title: 1996 AHSME Problem 15
statement: Two opposite sides of a rectangle are each divided into \(n\) congruent segments, and the endpoints of one segment are joined to the center to form triangle \(A.\) The other sides are each divided into \(m\) congruent segments, and the endpoints of one of these segments are joined to the center to form triangle \(B.\) [See figure for \(n=5,\) \(m=7.\)] What is the ratio of the area of triangle \(A\) to the area of triangle \(B?\)

solutions.text: Triangle \(A\) has base \(\frac{w}{n}\) and altitude \(\frac{h}{2},\) so its area is \(\frac{wh}{4n}.\) Triangle \(B\) has base \(\frac{h}{m}\) and altitude \(\frac{w}{2},\) so its area is \(\frac{wh}{4m}.\) Their ratio is \(\frac{m}{n},\) and the correct answer is B.
hints: Write the rectangle’s side lengths as \(w\) and \(h\)
Each triangle has a base that is one divided segment and an altitude equal to half the opposite side length
